text: Each service keeps Flyway's default history table flyway_schema_history inside its own schema, and the migration-run record keeps the legacy Job fields (service, schema, version, checksum, drift result, startedAt, endedAt, status APPLIED or FAILED)
why: The target rule is one Flyway sequence per service but no source document names the history table a service uses or the field list of the run record; the as-built name flyway_schema_history_recovery belongs to the single recovery schema and cannot be reused by 19 services
read: Template and Rules v1 section R4 and section R5.5 DP-15; Architecture v5 slide 29; legacy story RWB-E1-044 sections 11, 12 and 13
confirm: Platform template owner confirms the history table name and the run-record fields
impact: The preserved story keeps the as-built table unchanged; the delta stories can build against the default table name and the legacy Job shape without waiting

text: Every service starts its own sequence at V0001 in its own migration folder, and the 19 baselines have no cross-service order because no migration of one service can depend on another service's schema
why: No source document gives the baseline order or the sequence start across the 19 services; the legacy four-digit merge-order rule applied to one folder only
read: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-15; Architecture v5 slide 29 (no cross-schema keys); legacy story RWB-E1-044 section 13 (D-RCV-28)
applied_in: RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2 section 11 and section 13; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON section 8
confirm: Solution architect confirms the sequence start per service and the absence of a cross-service baseline order
impact: Each service can start building its own baseline on Day 1; only a cross-service data dependency would need a new ruling

why: No source document gives the contract location or says whether the platform template or each service owns the Flyway module; the as-built package recovery.casewf.migration has no target equivalent
read: Architecture v5 slides 29 and 38; Template and Rules v1 section R8.1; legacy story RWB-E1-044 sections 12 and 13
applied_in: RWB-PLT-E1044-CON section 10 and section 13; RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2 section 3
confirm: Platform template owner confirms the contract location and the module ownership
impact: The contract and the module are built once for all 19 services; a move later changes the path and not the rules

why: The legacy flag and the run output exist but no source document gives the record fields as a deployment contract, the alert threshold, or the flag owner after the split of the monolith module into 19 services
